title: Config
description:
The `config.toml` document.

Unknown sections and unknown keys inside a known section are ignored, so a file written for a
newer ocx degrades to the parts an older one understands; the cost is that a typo'd key
silently does nothing. A change that cannot degrade (a key whose meaning or value shape
changed) ships as a managed payload under a new OCI tag, and fleets move onto it as they
upgrade — see "Rolling out an incompatible change" in the user guide.

registries.description:
Named per-registry configuration tables (`[registries.<name>]`).

Every key is an identifier prefix, always — `[registry] default`
never dereferences through this table. The key is the package name's
domain, not the host serving the bytes: an entry keyed on the host
matches no package, so its `trusted_hosts` never applies.

mirrors.description:
Per-traffic-host mirrors (`[mirrors."<host>"]`).

Maps a canonical upstream traffic host (e.g. `"ghcr.io"`, `"index.ocx.sh"`) to replacement
endpoint(s), so read traffic goes to a corporate mirror instead of a blocked origin. A bare
string rewrites both traffic roles for that host; a `{registry?, index?}` table splits per
role — `registry` rewrites OCI distribution traffic only, `index` index-tree traffic only.

Replace semantics: no origin fallback. The canonical identifier and content-addressed digest
stay unchanged, so an `ocx.lock` produced behind the mirror remains valid with direct egress
and vice versa.

patches.description:
Site-tier patch configuration (`[patches]`).

Points at an operator-controlled patch registry that provides companion
packages, such as CA bundles, proxy env vars and license-server endpoints.
They are layered onto unmodified upstream packages at compose time.

Absent → no patch tier configured (opt-in, not required).

managed.description:
Corporate managed-configuration tier (`[managed]`).

Points at an operator-controlled OCI artifact that supplies a plain
`config.toml` payload, such as mirrors, a patches pointer and a default
registry. The payload is synced into local state and merged above the
user config every invocation.

Absent → no managed tier configured (opt-in, seeded by
`ocx self setup --managed-config`).

update.description:
Background update checks (`[update]`): the posture for OCX itself and for the toolchain,
plus the interval between checks.

A personal setting, read from `config.toml` only: a managed payload's `[update]` is
ignored and an `ocx.toml` refuses it. An unknown value never fails a command.

trust.description:
Identity-pinned verification policies (`[[trust.policy]]`).

Unlike every other section, trust policies **array-append** across the `config.toml` tiers
rather than replace — the operator trust set is the union of system, user and `$OCX_HOME`.
At verify time this operator set takes precedence over the project `ocx.toml`.

Consumed by `ocx package verify`.

sigstore.description:
Sigstore instances (`[sigstore."<authority>"]`): the trust material and endpoints of each Fulcio and Rekor
stack a keyless signer can name.

Read from `config.toml` tiers only: a repository that could name its own Fulcio CA would verify its own
signatures. Tables merge per table and per field, last tier wins; a table under `fulcio.sigstore.dev`
overrides the built-in public instance field by field.

shell.description:
Shell-integration settings (`[shell]`) — the per-prompt hook and
completions toggles, plus the activation consent whitelist.

**Never read from a project's `ocx.toml`**, only from `config.toml`
tiers: consent read from a repository's own file would let a clone
consent to itself. Consumed by `ocx self activate`, `ocx self setup`
and `ocx shell state`.

records.description:
Execution-record sink (`[records]`).

Designates where OCX writes one JSON resolution record per tool launch —
the resolved package closure with digests, plus the resolved executable.
Declared in the system tier it clamps: no lower tier can redirect or
disable it.

Absent → no records written (opt-in).

telemetry.description:
OpenTelemetry export settings (`[telemetry]`).

Declared in the system tier it clamps: no lower tier can redirect or disable export.

Absent → no telemetry is exported (opt-in).

blobs.description:
Blob directories and the blob cache (`[blobs]`).

Read from `config.toml` tiers only: a project's `ocx.toml` refuses it and the loader strips
it from a project tier. Not lockable, so `OCX_NO_CONFIG` drops it.

Absent → no blob directories and no blob cache.

toolchain_dir.description:
Root directory holding every project's toolchain tree, each at `<root>/<project-key>/toolchain/`.

The global toolchain tree ignores this key, and the directory need not exist yet.

extra_ca_certs.description:
Path to a PEM file of extra CA certificate(s), trusted for OCI registry, index and forge
traffic in addition to the platform trust store.

A relative path resolves against the directory of the `config.toml` that declared it.

Overridden by the `OCX_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` environment variable, which outranks every
`config.toml` tier unless the pair is declared in the system tier.

extra_ca_certs_pem.description:
The extra CA certificate bundle inlined verbatim (PEM text).

This is the form a fleet receives; `ocx config push` inlines a path-form `extra_ca_certs` here.

RegistryDefaults.description:
Global registry-subsystem settings (`[registry]` section).

Unknown keys are ignored, like in every other `config.toml` table.

default.description:
Default registry for bare identifiers (e.g. `nodejs/node:24` expands to
`<default>/nodejs/node:24`).

Overridden by the `OCX_DEFAULT_REGISTRY` environment variable. Always a
literal prefix (e.g. `"ghcr.io"`, `"ocx.sh"`) — never resolved through
the `[registries.<name>]` table.

RegistryConfig.description:
Configuration for a single `[registries.<name>]` entry.

Unknown keys are ignored, like in every other `config.toml` table.

index.description:
Base URL of the `index.ocx.sh`-protocol index this namespace resolves through, e.g.
`"https://index.ocx.sh"`, or `file:///absolute/path` for a local index read with no server.

**Field presence is the kind marker.** An entry that carries `index` resolves via the
ocx-index protocol; one without it, or no entry at all, resolves as plain OCI, with no
fallback. A `file://` base is checked at startup: a relative path or a remote authority is refused.

`index = ""` resolves the namespace as plain OCI. A `[mirrors]` registry entry for the
namespace in a config file you control suppresses the compiled-in index; the managed tier
and `OCX_MIRRORS` cannot.

trusted_hosts.description:
SSRF escape hatch for this namespace's physical registry hosts. Each
entry is an exact hostname or a CIDR block whose resolved addresses skip
the default-on private/loopback/link-local/metadata refusal.

A hostname entry also lets `ocx package prune --forge github` delete through the GitHub
Enterprise packages API of a `containers.<host>` registry that this namespace's index names.
Only an exact hostname vouches for that; a CIDR block does not.

insecure.description:
Contact this registry over plain HTTP instead of HTTPS.

Unioned with `OCX_INSECURE_REGISTRIES`, except that a system-tier entry stating
`insecure = false` locks that host shut against the env list too.

signatures.description:
Whether packages of this registry must carry publisher identities declared in the index.

One of `if_declared` (verify when the package declares publishers), `required` (refuse a package without
them) or `off` (skip the check). Defaults to `if_declared`. An unknown value is treated as `required`,
with one warning per run.

A lock-first install in a fresh home makes no index request, so it installs without the publisher check.
Set `required` to check those installs too: a package whose committed root declares no publishers is
then refused (exit 81, `publishers_required`), and the error names `ocx index update`.

index_publishers.description:
The signers allowed to sign this registry's index, in the shape of an index `publishers` array.

Replaces the built-in list for the registry. Entries are kept raw here and compiled where the index is
checked, so a malformed entry fails at that point.

index_signature.description:
Whether this registry's index must carry a valid signature: `off`, `warn` or `enforce`.

Defaults to `warn` for `ocx.sh`, which has a built-in signer list, and for any registry that sets
`index_publishers`; every other registry defaults to `off`. `enforce` needs a signer list.

`enforce` cannot hold for a namespace a local registry-role `[mirrors."<namespace>"]` entry pulls
off its index: that combination is refused with exit 78. The table key must be spelled as clients
spell the registry (lowercase, port as typed), or the entry is never applied.

index_expiry.description: Whether an expired index catalog is refused: `check` or `ignore`. Defaults to `check`.

anyOf.description: Verify against the index-declared publishers when the package declares any (the default).
Refuse a package whose index declares no publishers.

oneOf.description: Do not check the index signature.
Check it and log one warning per source on any failure, then continue.
Check it and refuse on any failure.

MirrorConfig.description:
Normalized `[mirrors."<host>"]` entry: one independent optional endpoint
per traffic role.

registry.description:
Endpoint for OCI distribution traffic (`/v2`) to this host, if a
registry role was declared for it (a bare string, `{registry: ...}`,
or `{registry: ..., index: ...}`).

index.description:
Endpoint for index-tree traffic (`/config.json`, `/c`, `/p`) to this
host, if an index role was declared for it.

PatchConfig.description:
Configuration for the `[patches]` tier.

Unknown keys are ignored, like in every other `config.toml` table.

registry.description:
OCI registry hosting patch descriptors, e.g.
`"internal.company.com/ocx-patches"`.

Absent → no patch tier configured.

path.description:
Path-template for per-package patch repositories. Default: `"{registry}/{repository}"`.

Placeholders: `{registry}` — the base identifier's registry host, slugified (characters
outside `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` become `_`); `{repository}` — the base identifier's repository path.

required.description:
Fail posture when a matched companion is unavailable.

- `true` (default) — fail closed: abort launch if a required companion
  cannot be resolved.
- `false` — fail open: skip with a warning (suitable for non-security
  companions like a license-server URL or metrics endpoint).

source.description:
OCI reference for the managed-config artifact, e.g.
`"internal.company.com/ocx-config:user"`.

Absent → no managed tier configured. The `OCX_MANAGED_CONFIG` environment variable
overrides it for one invocation.

required.description:
Fail posture when the snapshot is required but absent.

- `true` (default) — fail closed: a config error (exit 78) until `ocx config update`
  (or `self setup --managed-config`) syncs one.
- `false` — the tier contributes nothing until synced; a throttle-gated
  stderr hint only.

refresh.description:
Background refresh posture. Defaults to `notify`.

`apply` swaps in a drifted snapshot, `notify` advises `ocx config update`, `manual`
refreshes only on `ocx config update`. CI never runs the background check.

An unknown value is ignored with a warning, so the default applies.

interval.description:
Background refresh throttle interval, `\d+[smhd]?` (bare = seconds).
Defaults to `"1d"`.

RefreshPolicy.description: What a background check does when it finds drift.

oneOf.description:
A change is applied without asking, by the background check only, which runs only on an
interactive terminal, outside CI, and online.
A change prints a stderr notice naming the command that applies it; the check probes the registry but applies nothing.
The background check is skipped entirely; only an explicit command refreshes.

self.description:
What OCX does when a newer OCX is published: `apply` installs it after the command
finishes, `notify` (default) prints a notice, `manual` never checks.
Overridden by the `OCX_SELF_UPDATE` environment variable.

toolchain.description:
What OCX does when a locked tool's tag has moved: `notify` (default) prints a notice,
`manual` never checks. `apply` is treated as `notify`: only `ocx update` moves a pin.
Overridden by the `OCX_TOOLCHAIN_UPDATE` environment variable.

oneOf.description: Read as `notify`: only `ocx update` moves a pin.
A change prints a stderr notice naming the command that applies it; the check probes the registry but applies nothing.
The background check is skipped entirely; only an explicit command refreshes.

interval.description:
Minimum time between two checks, `\d+[smhd]?` (bare digits = seconds); `"0"` checks on
every command. Defaults to `"1d"`. Overridden by the `OCX_UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL`
environment variable.

TrustConfig.description: Container for the `[trust]` config section (`[[trust.policy]]` entries).

policy.description: The declared policies. Empty when `[trust]` is present but lists none.

TrustPolicy.description:
A single `[[trust.policy]]` entry.

One `signers` array names everyone this policy accepts, each entry tagged
`kind = "keyless"` or `kind = "key"`. Acceptance is ANY-of, so **adding a
signer always widens what verifies, never narrows it**.

```toml
[[trust.policy]]
scope = "ghcr.io/acme/*"
# or, to carve a subtree back out:
# scope = { include = ["ghcr.io/acme/*"], exclude = ["ghcr.io/acme/experimental/*"] }

signers = [
  { kind = "keyless",
    identity = "https://github.com/acme/tool/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v1.2.3",
    oidc_issuer = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" },
]
```

A policy left with no usable signer (an absent or empty `signers`, only unknown `kind`s, or a
misspelled field that parses as an unknown key) is refused and fails closed, never widening.

scope.description:
Which packages this policy applies to: one prefix pattern, or an include/exclude set of them.

A pattern matches on `/`-separated path-segment boundaries, and an absent scope is a catch-all.

```toml
scope = "ghcr.io/acme/*"
scope = { include = ["ghcr.io/acme/*"], exclude = ["ghcr.io/acme/experimental/*"] }
```

builder.description:
Expected SLSA provenance builder identity, matched against the
provenance predicate during attestation verify.

Ignored in signature mode, without an error.

signers.description:
The signers this policy accepts: an **ANY-of** set, each entry tagged
`kind = "keyless"` or `kind = "key"`.

```toml
signers = [
  { kind = "keyless", identity = "release@acme.example", oidc_issuer = "https://accounts.google.com" },
  { kind = "key",     key = "etc/acme-release.pub" },
]
```

**Every added entry widens what verifies**, and an empty set is a configuration error, not a
catch-all.

oneOf.description: One scope pattern. Segment-bounded without a `*`, literal-prefix glob with one; the empty string is a catch-all.
Patterns to cover, minus patterns to carve back out. A target matches when it matches at least one `include` (an empty `include` is a catch-all) and no `exclude`.

include.description: Patterns the policy covers. Empty is a catch-all.

exclude.description: Patterns carved back out. Beats `include` wherever both match.

SignerSpec.description:
One entry of a policy's `signers = [...]` array, tagged on `kind` with the
signer's fields flat beside the tag:

```toml
[[trust.policy]]
scope = "ghcr.io/acme/*"
signers = [
  { kind = "keyless", identity = "release@acme.example", oidc_issuer = "https://accounts.google.com" },
  { kind = "key", key = "etc/acme-release.pub" },
]
```

An empty array is a configuration error, never a catch-all.

oneOf.description:
A `kind` this build does not know — an entry written by a newer OCX.

It narrows: it accepts nobody, and a sibling `keyless` entry in the same
policy keeps working. A policy whose signers are *all* unknown is refused
with an error naming it.

SigstoreAuthority.description: A Sigstore instance name: the lowercase `host[:port]` of its Fulcio, without scheme or path. A `:443` port is dropped.

KeylessMatcher.description:
A `kind = "keyless"` signer: which Sigstore identity may sign.

Exactly one of `identity` / `identity_regexp` must be set — both or neither
is a configuration error — and `oidc_issuer` must be present.

identity.description:
Exact expected certificate SAN (byte-equal).

Mutually exclusive with `identity_regexp`.

identity_regexp.description:
Regex the certificate SAN must match in full (anchored `\A…\z`).

Mutually exclusive with `identity`.

claims.description:
Fulcio certificate claims that must all match, keyed by claim name or raw OID.

Every listed claim must match, and values compare as exact strings. A key is a known claim name
(`build_signer_uri`, `source_repository_identifier`, `source_repository_owner_identifier`,
`build_trigger`, `build_signer_digest`) or a raw OID under `1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.`; an unknown
name matches nobody.

Alone or beside `identity` / `identity_regexp`.

sigstore.description:
The Sigstore instance this signer trusts, named by the authority of its Fulcio (`host[:port]`).

Absent means the public instance, `fulcio.sigstore.dev`. The matching `[sigstore."<authority>"]` table
supplies the trust root.

KeyMatcher.description:
The `kind = "key"` signer: one public key, by reference or inline.

Exactly one of `key` / `key_pem` must be set. There is no `key_regexp`: a
public key is a fixed value, not a pattern.

`ocx config push` inlines the reference form into `key_pem` at publish time.

key.description:
A key reference (`[scheme://]<rest>`), the same spelling `--key` takes on the command line.

Mutually exclusive with `key_pem`, and refused in a managed-config payload.

key_pem.description:
Verbatim SPKI PEM.

Mutually exclusive with `key`.

SigstoreInstances.description: The configured `[sigstore."<authority>"]` tables, keyed by instance.

SigstoreInstance.description:
One `[sigstore."<authority>"]` table: where verification and signing get their trust material for one
instance.

Every field is optional. No `deny_unknown_fields`: a table written for a newer ocx degrades to its known parts.

trusted_root.description:
Path to a Sigstore trusted-root JSON, or a directory holding `trusted_root.json`.

A relative path resolves against the directory of the `config.toml` that declared it.
Mutually exclusive with `trusted_root_json`.

trusted_root_json.description:
The trusted-root document inlined verbatim; the form a fleet receives from `ocx config push`.
Mutually exclusive with `trusted_root`.

fulcio_url.description: Fulcio base URL. Its authority must equal the table key; absent, it defaults to `https://<key>`.

rekor_url.description: Rekor base URL, needed only to sign with a Rekor upload.

rekor_upload.description:
Whether a key-mode signature is uploaded to the transparency log when neither `--rekor-upload` nor
`--no-rekor-upload` is given. Keyless signing always uploads and ignores this field.

ShellConfig.description:
The `[shell]` section.

Unknown keys are ignored, like in every other `config.toml` table — except inside
`[shell.consent]`, which refuses them.

hook.description:
Whether the per-prompt shell hook runs.

`--hook` / `--no-hook` and a truthy `OCX_NO_HOOK` take precedence; absent means it
follows session interactivity. A higher tier's value wins in either direction, the managed
tier over a user's own file included.

completions.description:
Whether shell completions load, with the same precedence as `hook`:
`--completion` / `--no-completion` and a truthy `OCX_NO_COMPLETION` win.

modify_path.description:
Whether `ocx self setup` may write PATH surfaces — shell profiles and
the session-PATH stores alike. Absent means true.

profiles.description:
Which shell profile files receive the managed OCX block.

Absent means auto-detect fresh on every run; an empty list means write
no profile blocks at all.

ShellConsent.description:
The `[shell.consent]` table.

Unknown keys are refused here, unlike every other `config.toml` table: a host that meets a
future narrowing key it does not know **refuses** the payload rather than silently dropping the
key and activating on the full namespace.

paths.description:
Directories that activate unconditionally, modelled on git's `safe.directory`.

An entry is one exact directory, or with a trailing `/*` that directory and everything
beneath it, matched component-wise. A bare `*` grants nothing.

Entries are compared **literally**, after separator and trailing-slash normalization,
against the canonical project directory; an entry naming a symlinked checkout never matches.
A **leading** `~` expands textually against the home directory.

A `paths` grant is drift-blind and writes no stamp, so revoking it is immediate.

namespaces.description:
Source namespaces that activate a project whose whole lock is inside them.

One pattern, or one `{include, exclude}` table where `exclude` beats `include`, so
"everything under `ocx.sh/acme/*` except the one compromised namespace" is spellable.

oneOf.description: One consent pattern. Segment-bounded without a `*`, literal-prefix glob with one; the empty string drops the `[shell.consent]` table with a warning.
Patterns to cover, minus patterns to carve back out. A source matches when it matches at least one `include` and no `exclude`.

include.description: Patterns the policy covers. Required in the table form; an empty list drops the `[shell.consent]` table with a warning.

exclude.description: Patterns carved back out. Beats `include` wherever both match.

RecordsOptions.description: Where and how execution records are written.

dir.description:
Directory records are written to. Absent → recording is off.

Overridden by the `--records-dir` flag and the `OCX_RECORDS_DIR` environment variable.

name.description:
Name template for each record file, e.g. `{time}-{host}-{pid}-{rand}.json`.

Must contain a component that varies per record, or two frames sharing a
sink resolve to one path. Defaults to `{time}-{pid}-{rand}.json`.
Overridden by the `--records-name` flag and the `OCX_RECORDS_NAME` environment variable.

required.description:
Fail posture when a record cannot be written.

`true` aborts the launch; `false` warns and proceeds. **Config-file only at every tier** —
never settable from the environment or a flag.

Defaults `false` unlocked, `true` when SYSTEM-locked.

TelemetryConfig.description: Where and how OpenTelemetry log records are exported.

enabled.description: Turns export on (`true`) or off (`false`). Absent → export stays off.

endpoint.description:
Base URL of the OTLP/HTTP collector, an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host and no
user information. `/v1/logs` is appended to its path.

headers.description:
HTTP headers sent with every export, typically an authorization token.

Names must be HTTP tokens other than `host`, `content-length`, `content-type`,
`transfer-encoding`, `connection`, `keep-alive`, `proxy-connection`, `te`, `trailer` and
`upgrade`; values must not contain CR, LF or NUL. Values are secrets. A layer that sets
`endpoint` discards the headers inherited from earlier layers.

timeout.description: Export deadline in milliseconds, `1` to `10000`. Defaults to `500`.

protocol.description: Wire protocol. Only `http/protobuf` is supported, which is also the default.

service_name.description: Replaces the `service.name` resource attribute. Must not be empty.

resource_attributes.description: Extra resource attributes added to every export, keyed by a non-empty attribute name.

HeaderValue.description:
A header value sent with every telemetry export. Always a secret: it never appears in `Debug`
output, a log line or an error message.

BlobsConfig.description: Where ocx looks for blobs before it contacts a registry, and where it keeps the ones it fetches.

dirs.description:
Directories searched, read-only, for blobs before a registry is contacted.

A relative path resolves against the directory of the `config.toml` that declared it, and the
`[managed]` tier accepts absolute paths only. A later tier replaces this list whole. More
than 32 entries are refused (exit 78). Overridden by the `OCX_BLOB_DIR` environment variable and the
`--blob-dir` flag.

cache_dir.description:
Directory where blobs fetched from a registry are kept for later runs. Absent → no blob cache.

A relative path resolves against the directory of the `config.toml` that declared it.
Overridden by the `OCX_BLOB_CACHE_DIR` environment variable and the `--blob-cache-dir` flag.
